fullPassage:
Perfectly shaped tomatoes grow under purple lighting. Here in the facility, the intensity and timing of light and the nutrients in the water supply are all controlled. This indoor vertical farming facility is able to produce fresh fruit and vegetables all year round.
Vertical farming refers to producing foods in vertically stacked layers integrated into other structures, usually without the need of soil or natural light. Since the plants are stacked above each other, it reduces the amount of space needed to grow crops.
Another advantage of indoor vertical farming is that maintaining the ideal conditions can reduce the time to harvest. "For traditional farming, if the climate is good, you have five to six harvests a year," says the manager of the facility. "In indoor farming, we're now getting roughly 17 harvests out of that same period."
There is also the benefit of a reduced need for water. Any excess water that a plant cannot absorb will drop down to the plants below. The manager says the farm uses 95% less water than farming in a field. "Every time water moves through the system, it's captured and reused."
However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles' heel: energy consumption. It has been criticized for the high energy input it requires. "Solar power could help bring down energy costs," the manager says. "Large scale farms will have solar panels on each roof. It might support 10 to 15% of our needs."
This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather than replace outside fields. "Much of our fruit and vegetables will still be grown under the sun and in soil, which is why it is super important that we also invest in sustainable field farming," the manager says.

questions.passage: Perfectly shaped tomatoes grow under purple lighting. Here in the facility, the intensity and timing of light and the nutrients in the water supply are all ①<u>controlled</u>. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ stacking → stacked. '수직으로 쌓인 층'에서 layers는 '쌓는' 것이 아니라 '쌓여진' 것(수동).
det.analysis:
① controlled: 수동태 'are all controlled' 정상
② producing: 'refers to + 동명사' 정상
③ stacking → stacked: layers가 수동적으로 쌓여진 상태 → 과거분사 ←정답
④ integrated: 과거분사 후치수식 정상
det.tip: stacked(쌓여진, 수동) vs stacking(쌓고 있는, 능동). layers는 쌓여지는 대상

questions.passage: "Every time water moves through the system, it's ①<u>capturing</u> and reused." There is also the benefit of a ②<u>reduced</u> need for water. The manager says the farm ③<u>uses</u> 95% less water than farming in a field. Any excess water ④<u>that</u> a plant cannot absorb will drop down to the plants below.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① capturing → captured. 'it's captured and reused'에서 it(물)은 포집되는 대상이므로 수동태 과거분사.
det.analysis:
① capturing → captured: 'it's captured and reused' — 수동태. 물이 포집되는 것 ←정답
② reduced: 과거분사 수식 'a reduced need' 정상
③ uses: 현재시제 3인칭 단수 정상
④ that: 주격 관계대명사 정상
det.tip: captured and reused = 포집되어 재사용 (수동태 병렬). it = water(물)

questions.passage: However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles' heel: energy consumption. It has been ①<u>criticized</u> for the high energy input it requires. "Solar power could help ②<u>bring</u> down energy costs," the manager says. This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather than ③<u>replace</u> outside fields. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ growing → grown. 'will still be grown'에서 과일과 채소는 '재배되는' 대상이므로 수동태.
det.analysis:
① criticized: 현재완료 수동태 'has been criticized' 정상
② bring: 'help + 동사원형' 정상
③ replace: 'rather than + 동사원형' 정상
④ growing → grown: 'will be grown'(미래 수동태). 과일/채소가 재배되는 것 ←정답
det.tip: will be + p.p. = 미래 수동태. grow-grew-grown. 과일/채소 = 재배되는 대상(수동)

questions.passage: Another advantage of indoor vertical farming is that maintaining the ①<u>ideal</u> conditions can reduce the time to harvest. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 식물이 흡수하지 못하는 초과(excess) 수분이 아래로 떨어진다. insufficient(부족한)는 excess의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ insufficient → excess: 원문은 'excess water'. insufficient(부족한)은 반대
❌ ① ideal: 원문 일치. 이상적인
❌ ② traditional: 원문 일치. 전통적인
❌ ③ reduced: 원문 일치. 줄어든
det.tip: excess(과잉의/초과의) ↔ insufficient(부족한)

questions.passage: However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles' heel: energy ①<u>consumption</u>. It has been ②<u>praised</u> for the high energy input it requires. det.korean: 높은 에너지 투입량으로 비판받아 왔다(criticized). praised(칭찬받은)는 반의어로 부적절.

❌ ③ panels: 원문 일치. 패널
❌ ④ needs: 원문 일치. 필요

questions.passage:
Perfectly shaped tomatoes grow under purple lighting. Here in <u>the</u> facility, the intensity and timing of light and the nutrients in the water supply are all controlled. This indoor vertical farming facility is able to produce fresh fruit and vegetables all year round.
Vertical farming refers to producing foods in vertically stacked layers integrated into other structures, usually without the need of soil or natural light. Since the plants are stacked above each other, it reduces the amount of space needed to grow crops.
Another advantage of indoor vertical farming is that maintaining the ideal conditions can reduce the time to harvest. "For traditional farming, if the climate is good, you have five to six harvests a year," says the manager of the facility. "In indoor farming, we're now getting roughly 17 harvests out of that same period."
There is also the benefit of a reduced need for water. Any excess water that a plant cannot absorb will drop down to the plants below. The manager says the farm uses 95% less water than farming in a field. "Every time water moves through the system, it's captured and reused."
However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles' heel: energy consumption. It has been criticized for the high energy input it requires. "Solar power could help bring down energy costs," the manager says. "Large scale farms will have solar panels on each roof. It might support 10 to 15% of our needs."
This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather than replace outside fields. "Much of our fruit and vegetables will still be grown under the sun and in soil, which is why it is super important that we also invest in sustainable field farming," the manager says.
